channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Canada to Provide Steel, Auto Sectors With Billions to Ease Trade Crunch
item.description: It is Canada’s latest dollop of federal aid for companies that have faced financial strain since President Trump imposed hefty tariffs on foreign-made metals and automotives.

item.title: Nine Ebola Cases Have Kenya Holding Its Breath
item.description: Health authorities are waiting to see whether their swift quarantine actions were enough to prevent a full-blown outbreak.

item.title: Witkoff’s Praise of Putin as ‘Humanitarian’ Tracks With U.S. Approach to Russia
item.description: The U.S. envoy’s remarks in Russia sparked fury among Ukraine’s supporters, but they follow President Trump’s strategy for ending the Ukraine war.

item.title: Congressional Candidate Brad Lander Says Israeli Military Detained Him in West Bank
item.description: The New York City Democrat was in the occupied territory accompanying Palestinians during an olive harvest.

item.title: Elon Musk’s Starlink Speed Cap Has Scrambled Ukraine’s Defenses
item.description: A slowdown in Ukraine’s military version of Starlink ordered by Musk is hurting Kyiv’s ability to stop Russian attacks.

item.title: Russia Releases Captured American in Sign of Warming Ties
item.description: Stephen Hubbard had been living in Ukraine for years at the time of his detention in 2022.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: What’s Behind the Protests in France and What Happens Next
item.description: Weeks of student-led protests over conditions in French schools have spiraled into violent protests across the country.

item.title: Chinese AI Tool Linked to Hacks in Japan
item.description: Around 80 Japanese companies were targeted from overseas in hacks that bore digital traces of Artex, an AI agent developed in China.

item.title: U.K. Inflation Jumps Again, Strengthening Case for Rate Hike
item.description: Inflation rose further above the Bank of England’s target as policymakers prepare for a meeting that is expected to yield a first rate increase since the start of the Iran war.

item.title: Musk Ordered Starlink Slowdown That Crippled Ukraine’s Drones and Sowed Panic in Kyiv
item.description: Plus, autism-therapy workers say big chains pressured them to boost treatment hours, and NYSE is getting trounced in the battle for Wall Street’s biggest IPOs.

item.title: Musk Ordered Starlink Slowdown That Blindsided Ukraine
item.description: The SpaceX founder authorized the move and has been discussing Ukraine with Trump, but the president has denied ordering the restrictions.

item.title: U.K. Government on Track to Cut Borrowing Ahead of Budget
item.description: The government cut borrowing in the first six months of its fiscal year—but at a slower pace than planned—underlining the challenges posed by rising prices and interest payments.

item.title: Airfield Attack Marked Opening Shot in Putin’s Stepped-Up Sabotage Campaign
item.description: The failed operation in eastern Germany this summer was part of a new wave of attacks ordered by President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: More Oil Is Now Coming Out of the Persian Gulf Than Before the Iran War
item.description: Experience and big paydays have created a more resilient tanker fleet. Oil traders worry it isn’t sustainable.

item.title: Alberta Voted to Stay in Canada but the Separatists Vow to Fight On
item.description: Some saw the referendum as giving oxygen to a movement that previously had only marginal support.

item.title: ‘The Mothers of Kherson’ Review: A Ukraine War Opera
item.description: A startlingly of-the-moment work about Russia’s abduction of children during the war in Ukraine, co-commissioned by the Metropolitan Opera, had its premiere in Warsaw last week.

item.title: Oil Futures Settle Lower in Volatile Session
item.description: Oil futures settled lower in a volatile session that saw prices reach multimonth highs before pulling back as traders considered prospects for U.S.-Iran diplomacy amid continuing Middle East supply risks.

item.title: French Police Hunt for Suspected Rioters in Weekend Unrest
item.description: Authorities are combing through security footage and social media as they look for those involved in looting and vandalism.

item.title: Trump Envoy Tells Nervous Gulf Allies U.S. Can’t Guarantee Security Forever
item.description: Tom Barrack’s message comes as countries in the Middle East worry the U.S. will leave them to clean up after the Iran war.
